gap-band-extremals.author: coordinator-20260921-round7
gap-band-extremals.locator: Round7 repaired proof, coordinate-aware regression and independent review
gap-band-extremals.content: Round7 reusable route: use a full-interval Volterra integral equation rather than a Taylor estimate restricted to a first block whose width may vanish. Weighted normalization transfers C1 convergence to a uniform endpoint slope gap. Root isolation then controls entire blocks, not only midpoint signs. A separate thin-heavy-interval construction combines n-dimensional low-energy platforms with a codimension-n central-zero subspace to prove the fixed-n supremum limit (n+1)^2*pi^2. The local formal Wronskian declarations in lean-proof/SL/AuditRound7.lean are linked through the round7 report, with actual type/axiom scope. This does not identify finite-R optimizers or prove all-R self-consistent branches. See the exact reviewed source and round7 report.

feynman-hellmann.author: coordinator-20260921-round7
feynman-hellmann.locator: Round7 repaired proof, coordinate-aware regression and independent review
feynman-hellmann.content: Round7 checking lesson: store the parameterization and normalization with every derivative. Nonstationary test points detect a missing mirror factor that every root-residual test misses. Fixed-space potential perturbations and variable-weight strings use different denominators. Full-interface Hessians require true matrix multiplication; away from stationarity retain the rank-one term. Local formal references: lean-proof/SL/AuditRound7.lean (mirrored_gap_from_single_interface, mirrored_stationarity_iff) checks scalar combination under explicit FH premises; see the round7 report for exact compiler and semantic receipts, not a full spectral differentiability theorem. The old op03_gap_precise eigenfunction backend has a confirmed propagator-order defect; current op03_gap_fh imports existing fixed and was checked on bounded examples. Historical callers and analytic spectral Jacobian backends are not globally certified by these finite tests.
